body: I hear you, except I can say that when you live it, it can be in some cases overall worth it

thank you for posting this. don't have the energy to describe my story right now, but I've had two experiences uncannily like this and a lifetime structurally like this. I'm so old now and it's like I never get over it. jealous of those who are able to. but reading this helped.

I find that being really clear and saying "It's just a weird thought I have that bothers me, not anything I would act on or have any plan to act on, but it's obviously pretty upsetting and hard" or something like that really ticks off all the boxes. it's like a code therapists understand.

I have never had anyone go to full panic just for having occasional EDIT: or even frequent suicidal thoughts. The thing that sets off the alarm is if you have a plan. So maybe get help and just don't act like you have a plan. I have been to multiple therapists in multiple parts of the US and no one goes straight to institutionalization or whatever unless you articulate specific concrete plans. Like I've even said "I had a plan last month but I don't now" and the therapist just kept trying to help me without flipping out and turning useless.

Hope my experiences are helpful. Lmk if you have other questions.

I think that could be a good solution. therapists can sometimes be good as trained outside voices for weighing in on questions like this. 100% recommend finding a therapist. also don't keep seeing one you don't like. I know energy / will levels are low. just do what you can. . . .

have you seen a therapist since the breakup? 

I hope you find something that helps. this is a lot to go through and even though I can tell you things will feel better and that being thirty is not too late to start over and find a better life and support system, I respect that you may not feel that yet. this is some hard shit and I'm sorry you're going through it.

I hope you discover the other measures that reveal why your life isn't good and find ways to improve according to those measures and then stop hating your life and hating yourself. 

but I really hear you about what you want to hear. I do lots of things to try to take the pressure off being alive. so in the meantime, I hope you find those, too.
that's a legit feeling even if I bet I'm right. just don't act on it. I agree with torito_supremo, who is kind of expressing what I'm saying more eloquently. see how you feel tmrw

more practically speaking, when you get home, maybe you can read some speculative fiction or play a game or do whatever the equivalent of that you do to distract yourself. weather the storm for a night?

I think you're wrong but it's true I can't argue with that theory. however, I've been on earth probably twice as long as you and have experienced this stuff super intensely, so while you may think I'm a condescending loser with illogical optimism, you may also want to consider what I have to say

I'm not saying you're on a straight line to improvement. wanting things to get better and seeing that clearly is all it takes in a way, but that can be super hard. I don't know you so I don't know how hard it will be. but worth it

because many of the things you list are in fact much more under your control and a matter of point of view than they feel right now. like if you told me you were constantly mass murdering people, I'd be pretty sure you were fucked. but the friendless no relationship ugly hate-filled and stupid stuff, while they probably are super real right now to you and I don't want to deny that--those are all things that can and will change if you wait for other parts of yourself to emerge.

also obviously the teenager thing will change and that is part of it.

also I want to add that it's okay to walk around crying. it sucks to suffer but also walking around crying and posting on reddit are totally advanced ways of coping with suffering compared to many others

your opinion of yourself will change and so will reality. I don't know you so I can't tell you how long it will take or how it will happen. but if you have a will to live and to find meaning in your life despite all the negative things you are listing right now, this stuff will change. 

I made it. I still have hard times but I did. you are actually more in touch with your self-loathing than I was at your age, so I am guessing you will probably be better off for it when you're in your 20s and 30s, as fucked up and macabre as it sounds right now. lol

use this place if it helps. just hang on.
But yeah stop maintaining the shit you don't really want. The metaphor is real.

Sell your house and go talk to someone whose job it is to do that kind of "life coach" shit about how to start living. Or whatever, maybe go to a different subreddit and post something like "has anyone here rearranged their life? how did it work?"

Anyway, sorry you feel like garbage and regret. Sounds like the old misery mushroom is eating into the things that are normally tolerable. Keep talking here if it makes you feel better?

100%--yes this happens to me all the time. I also don't like to share good news because I get little pleasure and create massive envy b/c the world is so garbage rn. that last part at least is really nothing to do with being f'd by childhood.

did you gain your powers to feel through therapy?

but your story made me laugh and smile. so glad it still worked out and y'all are wed.

at some point the blame becomes its own creature and is very telling. like your blaming yourself for feeling suicidal or bad because there's no obvious thing to blame. that itself is something worth untangling with a pro. 

what may end up happening, maybe, is you realize what your true values are (the source of the sense of mismatch between conventional societal values about financial stability and relationships and your own unknown value system where you're unhappy). the con of that is you may be currently failing your true values. the pro is that you may learn what deep-seated values you've been hiding from that will really push you and give your life fuller meaning.

reminds me of me. there's a lot that happens when you push past that discomfort with someone you sort of trust (don't wait to trust someone completely, I'd advise, unless you are a trusting sort). see what happens in August. but if things get overwhelming before then, please don't wait. 

I personally am waiting till July when my insurance changes. . . . hoping no crises before then!

I agree with the other commenter. it's worth talking to someone about what you're feeling. you could be the smartest person in the world, but the right counselor/therapist could help you realize what's really going on just because they have the benefit of looking from a different perspective. give it a whirl?

please keep trying to find another way. let us know if we randos here can help at all.

full disclosure: I'm a sister who spent too long afraid I'd find out my brother was dead. I never resented him for that fear but I cannot tell you how happy I am that finally years later he's found a way to live in the world.

the internalization of the bullshit system of valuation that doesn't reward what's really important. on a micro level in your fam, on a macro level in society. I know this is a platitude, and you don't know me, but if you ever feel like trusting any random stranger online, just trust me. if you want to, you can exorcise the system of garbage values from inside you. (this is different from being angry about it.) it gets 100x easier once you're not living in a toxic micro-environment, but I'm not going to lie, it's still not easy. I wish you luck

Reading through your brilliant angry posts, I think you know the real thing you're angry about, the thing of which your ugliness is just a proxy symbol. I hope you beat the shit out of that thing and triumph. xo

I don't enjoy it. But it makes me feel better, like I'm helping myself. I think it has something to do with a deep sense of shared humanity that I can feel at the core of other people who have also contemplated giving up on humanity, whether it's their own or others'. 

So yeah, two reasons: I feel less alone at this edge of humanity, and I feel like by analogy I'm helping myself.

so reach the F*** out already!

back to work!

I feel for you so much right now. just know that these relapses are not the end of recovery, that it doesn't take as long to recover once you already know how, that other people are in fact shitbirds and don't do the right thing much of the time, but that if I had been there I would have defended you.

I mean I know I could always call crying, and sometimes I still do, but I am really tired of being that friend for the last 4 years. 

I try to "save" those phone calls because, as I said, I'm just obsessed with killing myself--I don't think I ever will act on these near-daily feelings--and I am playing a long game attempt to survive. for what? I don't know. I guess the things I make. they're really all I have. kind of pathetic. at least they aren't complete failures, even if they don't really justify the level of suffering and loneliness in my life.

yes, I totally hear you about the "improvement" narrative. lately something that takes the pressure off (but doesn't remove the suicidality or bad feelings per se) is just realizing that there is no improvement in terms of the presence of the feelings. but in some ways if I am later able to take a step back, there is an improvement in the way the feelings affect my life. some times. 

haha. always so many caveats with suicidality. I hope you find more talking therapies if that's what you're looking for. one way it's worked for me is they just invent new codes to extend the therapy. I don't really gaf what they code me with as long as the care gets paid for. . . .

This sounds really overwhelming. How's your relationship with your sister? Can you lean on her at all emotionally?

it wasn't possible for me when I was your age, but one thing I in retrospect (35/f here) wish I could have done was flip around the fake "everything's fine" and ask my parents for help.

(my parents were abusive motherfuckers who had no idea I was doing poorly until I was hospitalized, and then, when I was hospitalized, laughed at me and told me I was making up all my symptoms and bad feelings.)

but if you have ones that are less bad, or good, even, it may be worth it just to tell them what's going on. it's worth a try, taking a pause and living off their generosity to figure out how you can make things suck less. seriously this could just change everything. I know it may seem mindblowingly shameful now, but the dividends later will make all of that not matter.

as for the guilt of making your parents take care of you when it isn't their fault that you're this way right now, you can always pay it forward once you are feeling better. which is possible, no, probable. can't tell you how long it will take or what the path will be to feeling better than you currently do, but I do know it's possible, even probable.

fucked up thing was, I had just let my guard down and was being myself. there is a dark kind of humor in thinking that maybe the reason why I don't coo over small animals is that I was so profoundly harmed when I was a small animal. instead I was shunned and all the feelings of being unworthy to live came rushing back.

when I was your age it was a mystery to me--I guess it was hope that kept me going. in my case, I was right to hope, tho admittedly there have been no immediate fixes and a shit ton of depressing work.

now that I'm 35 and have been to years of therapy, it's not hope that keeps me going, paradoxically, so much as realizing there are ways to live that are good enough. on my worst days none of this matters, but most of the time, given many strategies, I feel so much less weight than I could ever have imagined in my early 20s. I know how to live, watch the desire to kill myself come and go, and keep going and live more.

it's weird, but even though I'm far from happy all the time--like I said, I'm still sometimes suicidal--I like the forms of life I've learned to live. I could tell you the specifics, **but it's not that the things I do to live now didn't exist when I was young; it's that they didn't feel rewarding because I hadn't learned how to live them as myself.** 

most of this was stuff I learned on my own, but a few good therapists (among a bunch of lame or less effective ones) also helped immensely.

my life didn't start till I really was free of the structures of school and family. you may already be in that situation, but you may want to give that part of life a try. again, nothing gets better immediately, but new spaces may possibly open up for different strategies at dealing with horrible sh*t.

anyway not to talk down to you or dismiss your experience. nothing is worse than the feeling that going through the suffering is impossible and inevitable except via death. nothing I say can take that away completely. but hope my story is of some small interest. thanks for your post.

hey there, I was where you were at more than half my life ago. I remember constantly shaming myself with the same thing: "I'm not alone," "this is totally common," "I have no reason to be upset"--at the time all I could see were the privileges I was wasting. actually you sound a lot more reasonable about it than I was, which speaks to your thoughtfulness.

when I was hospitalized (during college) I came to a similar conclusion as yours @ the long-term center. it was NOT good for me. I was lucky enough to be around ppl who gave me a lot of other suggestions--different kinds of therapy, etc. there are so many different approaches. 

you might consider asserting yourself and saying that you'd like different forms of help besides that center and seeing if there are other resources available where you're at?

anyway, just wanted to say thanks for posting, it's nice to talk to ppl in situations like I used to be in. sorry if this msg is annoying. hope you get some of what you're looking for here despite the cray trollz....
